When the flow has to wait

A dependency.
A pause.

An instruction may need a result that is still being computed. A stall gives it time. Forwarding can reduce that wait when the timing allows.

ADD R3, R1, R2→SUB R4, R3, R5

Working together.
Moving faster.

Fetch. Decode. Execute. Write.
Different instructions, progressing in the same cycle.

Start with the idea

Overlap
saves time.

While one instruction executes, another can decode and a third can be fetched. Each stage works on a different instruction during the same clock cycle.

5 instructions · 4 stages · 2 ns per stage

40 nsSequential

16 nsPipelined

2.5×Speedup

Equal stage times, no stalls, and no pipeline-register overhead. Pipelined time = (4 + 5 − 1) × 2 ns.
